Many of you have heard of the crazy Hawaiians protesting the Thirty Meter Telescope installation on Mauna Kea. I mean it’s silly, right? Natives protesting science on their sacred ground used historically by ancient Hawaiians for learning astronomy themselves. It makes for catchy headlines. But there is a story here that isn’t as sexy; a story that explains why people are there…and doesn’t come off condescending.

First of all, I’m not a reporter. Writing is not my trade. I’m merely frustrated at the media and their inherent bias. I also won’t reveal anyone’s identity, this is simply because I haven’t asked permission to quote anybody.

My friend, who is part Hawaiian, just finished his M.A. in Political Science; his father is an attorney and he himself was recently accepted into a well-known law school. I asked him if he supported the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle (an inside joke we have about the similarity of TMT to TMNT), his response made me actually sit down and think, “Fuck yeah, it’s going to bring jobs, tourists, money, science, and overall is pretty fucking cool”.

“Ok”, I replied, “then why the hell are you and your parents up there protesting?”

“We have to.” He replied. “My family is part of the Royal Order of Kamehameha. We are tasked by the constitution of the Hawaiian Kingdom to protect its sovereignty, we have no choice.”

Now, I’m the Kanaka Haole, or “local white native”, you see, I’m Hawaiian here points to head and here points to heart, 2 outta 3 aint bad and I can see where he’s coming from, but if you read his reply and thought, “well that’s stupid”, let me try to see if I can tell you why what he said struck home.

Everyone knows Hawai’i as the 50th state, but that’s probably all you know. You see the natives protesting and may say, “dude, get in line, we have Indians we fucked over well before we fucked you over.” But that’s not really the case. You see, one of the reasons we didn’t really care about screwing over the American Natives was because we never considered them to be sovereign. They did not have a flag (silly right?), they did not have recognizable forms of government, they did not have definitive borders, and they did not have international treaties and relations….Hawai’i had all of these. Hawai’i was an established Constitutional Monarchy with quite a few international treaties…they were a globally recognized sovereign state. Where Indians are displaced bands of people, Hawai’i is still, technically, (and this is recognized by the UN today) an occupied sovereign country.

“Whoa, hold up son”, you may ask, “wtf? This is news to me…I’ve never heard of this…didn’t US Congress pass a law about Hawai’i being a state?” Well, yes, but it is no different than if Congress would pass a law TODAY recognizing Russia as the new 51st state. Sounds silly with Russia, but tell me how it’s any different with Hawai’i.

Ok, nevermind, I’ll tell you how it’s different, here’s the basic nutshell version that loses a lot of details in the process: Some Haole (White) guy back in the day got cozy with a US military warship carrying US troops, he decided these Islands should become US property, he himself was a private civilian. He convinced the soldiers to storm the Hawaiian Kingdom Palace; the queen at the time was like, “WTF?? This fahking Haole, ok, fine, this is bullshit, but nobody wants bloodshed. These are, after all, US Soldiers and we have good relations with the US. I’m going to sign over JUDICIAL and LEGISLATIVE powers to the US and allow them to deal and punish their people as they see fit so as not to start an international incident, but I’m also including expiration dates on these powers and am retaining EXECUTIVE powers.”

Now Hawai’i is a US state.

If this jump is a little confusing, you may want to consult with some of the work that Dr. Sai has done in researching and tracking down some of these historical documents. Here’s a link to his page with his CV and more detailed information if you’re interested.

Anyway, the Royal Order of Kamehameha is a constitutionally (Hawaiian) recognized knighthood tasked “to promote and defend the sovereignty of the Kingdom of Hawai’i”. Some of the more cleverereer readers may start to see the political angle here: this is a huge opportunity for them to come out and say, “Hey guys, remember us?” The Royal Order has been gaining traction all over the state over the last few years. They march in parades, they hold events, and they consist of some very prominent people. This TMT situation is an opportunity for them to flex their political power, and they are jumping on it. Unfortunately, the media isn’t covering this side of the story, it’s too real and it has consequences. A “Crazy Hawaiians Hate Science” headline is better clickbait.

Now, whether or not you agree with the UN or Royal order doesn’t matter, because as my Hawaiian friend from earlier also said, and I’m paraphrasing, “KanakaHaole, this whole thing is just a fucking mess. The Kingdom of Hawaii is technically, by international law, still in existence and sovereign, but international law is bullshit because international law fundamentally undermines the sovereignty of every country. You can’t be sovereign and also be told what to do. The US is sovereign and militaristically strong. Hawaii is sovereign, and occupied. Laws are fake, they are only real if they are enforceable, and all that means is the person with the bigger stick tells the person with the smaller stick what to do; the US has a bigger stick than Hawai’i. It’s still my family’s constitutional duty to uphold our laws however and this is an excellent platform to do so publicly. Will we win? No. But it is still our duty to do what we do, would you roll over if China occupied the US? Would you look down at your kids and be proud of them for throwing your culture away because it was the easier course, or would you want to look down and see a little fiery fucker standing up for what’s his? It’s the principal of the matter; it’s not about the goddamned telescope.”

So that’s my story. It’s not everyone’s story, and there are certainly Hawaiians who DO NOT want a TMT up there, but it takes all kinds to make this world turn and now I have to decide whether I support my friends claim to HI sovereignty or my personal belief in scientific advancement. It’s a dirty choice, but we have a dirty history. I would love to hear voat’s thoughts on the issue.
